Haunted by 1971 torture
2014-03-25T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/haunted-by-1971-torture-17168

Kakan Bibi is now 90 but is still haunted by the trauma of torture the Pakistani forces inflicted on her for fighting against them in the 1971 Liberation War. The freedom fighter fought three front battles under sector-5 (Sylhet), and worked as an informant. She blew up a bridge throwing dynamite from a floating raft after male fighters failed to do this, she said. Speaking after inaugurating Shwadhinata Utshab-2014 as chief guest at Central Shaheed Minar in the capital yesterday, Kakan Bibi said it was the duty of the new generation to defend the country's independence. Sammilita Sangskritik Jote hosts the three-day festival at the Shaheed Minar and Rabindra Sharabar from March 24 to 26. Describing her heroics and brutality she suffered, she said the Pakistani army burnt her all her body with a heated iron rod, and marks of the torture were still there. "I used to do spying for sector-5 commander Mir Shawkat Ali and succeeded in providing information five times but I was caught by the Pakistani army on the sixth time and faced the brutality for around eight days," said Kakan. She said the Pakistani forces freed her when they knew she came to look for her husband who was an EPR member and she was a Khashi woman. Vice Chancellor of Dhaka University Prof AAMS Arefin Siddique, theatre personality Ramendu Majumdar, and eminent singer Fakir Alamgir addressed the programme.
